what: The heuristic precomputes all task-static CVRP information: customer indices, visited and loc fact mappings, current route load/vehicles variables, optional capacity/max-vehicles and customer demands (from exact numeric names or operator assignment effects), and directed/routing costs from grounded operator metric costs. During evaluation it reads the current state once into reusable buffers, builds the list of unvisited customers, and returns a finite non-negative nearest-neighbor greedy route-completion estimate. The estimator starts from the current vehicle location, load, and used-vehicle count; it repeatedly chooses the cheapest legal visit or visit-via-depot action for an unvisited customer, respects capacity and vehicle limits when those values are available, and finally adds the return-to-depot cost. If all customers are visited, it returns the remaining return-to-depot cost.
why: The remaining cost in CVRP is dominated by the route(s) needed to visit the remaining customers. Grounded operator metric costs provide a reliable, instance-independent way to reconstruct point-to-point and via-depot travel costs without fragile numeric-name parsing. A capacity- and vehicle-aware nearest-neighbor greedy completion is cheap to compute, captures the main constraints of the domain, and produces an informative non-admissible estimate. Precomputing static mappings and using reusable state buffers keeps per-evaluation work low, which is important because heuristic calls dominate search time.
